new.title: Walk the ramparts of medieval Guérande
new.desc: Guérande's walled old town has an enceinte of roughly 1.3 km with six towers and four gates. The Porte Saint-Michel, the best-known gate, holds medieval rooms, a temporary exhibition and access to the wall walk.
new.tip: Strolling the old town and around the walls is free; the Porte Saint-Michel visit is ticketed. Park outside the walls, as car access is restricted.
new.q: Porte Saint-Michel, Guérande

new.title: Step inside the Collégiale Saint-Aubin
new.desc: The former collegiate church on Place Saint-Aubin combines a 12th-century nave, a 15th-century choir and a 16th-century portal. It has been a listed monument since the 19th century and is under a ten-year restoration programme.
new.tip: Entry is free, with listed hours of 9:00-12:00 and 14:00-18:00. Scaffolding may be present during restoration works.
new.q: Collégiale Saint-Aubin, Place Saint-Aubin, Guérande

new.title: Climb the Saint-Guénolé tower in Batz-sur-Mer
new.desc: The 17th-century bell tower of the Saint-Guénolé church rises about 70 m above the village. From the top it overlooks the Guérande peninsula, the salt marshes and the ocean.
new.tip: Choose a clear day for the view across the salt pans. It is part of the heritage circuit of Batz's historic centre.
new.q: Tour Saint-Guénolé, Batz-sur-Mer

new.title: Discover the ruined Notre-Dame-du-Mûrier chapel
new.desc: This three-aisled chapel at 5 rue Mauperthuis in Batz-sur-Mer has been classed as a historic monument since 1862. Its ruined nave and columns are the starting point of the 1.3 km Historic Heart walk.
new.tip: Combine it with the church and the salt-marsh museum on the marked walk. The site is outdoors and free to look at.
new.q: Chapelle Notre-Dame-du-Mûrier, Rue Mauperthuis, Batz-sur-Mer

new.title: Wander the thatched hamlet of Kerhinet
new.desc: Kerhinet in Saint-Lyphard is a pedestrian hamlet of about 18 restored thatched cottages with two bread ovens, a well and a washing place. The Brière regional park bought and restored it in the 1970s.
new.tip: Park at the entrance and walk in. It also houses a visitor office, a craft shop and a weaver's workshop.
new.q: Village de Kerhinet, Saint-Lyphard

new.title: Explore the WWII submarine base of Saint-Nazaire
new.desc: Construction of the huge concrete U-boat base began in 1941 under the Organisation Todt. Today its pens can be visited freely and a rooftop terrace gives views over the port and the Loire estuary.
new.tip: Free access to the base; guided tours run daily in season from the tourist office. The base is on boulevard de la Légion d'Honneur.
new.q: Base sous-marine, Boulevard de la Légion d'Honneur, Saint-Nazaire

new.title: Board a full-size liner at Escal'Atlantic
new.desc: Inside two berths of the former submarine base, this museum rebuilds a transatlantic liner at full scale over about 3,500 square metres. It opened in 2000 and was redeveloped in 2013 by scenographers François Confino and François Seigneur.
new.tip: Allow one to one and a half hours. Check current prices and book ahead in high season.
new.q: Escal'Atlantic, Boulevard de la Légion d'Honneur, Saint-Nazaire

new.title: Admire the Saint-Nazaire bridge over the Loire
new.desc: Opened on 18 October 1975, this cable-stayed bridge links Saint-Nazaire to Saint-Brevin-les-Pins. Its steel section is about 720 m long with a 404 m central span, and with approach viaducts the crossing runs 3,356 m, the longest bridge in France.
new.tip: Best seen from the estuary waterfront in Saint-Nazaire or from the Mindin shore. Crossing is toll-free.
new.q: Pont de Saint-Nazaire, Saint-Nazaire

new.title: See the Serpent d'océan on the Mindin shore
new.desc: Huang Yong Ping's 130 m aluminium sea-serpent skeleton was inaugurated on 20 June 2012 for the Estuaire exhibition. It lies on the foreshore at Nez de Chien, half out of the water at low tide and submerged at high tide.
new.tip: Visit at low tide to walk beside it. It is reached along the Mindin shore path in Saint-Brevin-les-Pins and is free.
new.q: Serpent d'océan, Plage de Mindin, Saint-Brevin-les-Pins

new.title: Visit the Bluebeard castle of Pornic
new.desc: The Château de Pornic is a 15th-century fortress turned seaside residence, nicknamed the Bluebeard castle because it once belonged to Gilles de Rais. The Vogüé family has owned it since 1886 and it overlooks the old port.
new.tip: The castle is private, so book the guided interior visit or garden tour through the tourist office. Dates and prices change by season.
new.q: Château de Pornic, Rue du Château, Pornic

new.title: Roam the ruined fortress of Clisson
new.desc: The Château de Clisson was built by the Clisson family from the 12th century and strengthened by Duke François II of Brittany in the 15th century. It was burned in 1793 during the Vendée War and kept as a ruin after Lemot bought it in 1807.
new.tip: Open May to September (daily in July-August). Guided tours run from February to December.
new.q: Château de Clisson, Place du Minage, Clisson

new.title: Stroll through the Italianate Garenne Lemot
new.desc: This 13-hectare landscape park was created in the early 19th century by sculptor François-Frédéric Lemot. It contains the Villa Lemot, follies such as the Rocher Rousseau and the Grotte d'Héloïse, and runs along the Sèvre Nantaise. It was classed a historic monument in 1988.
new.tip: The main entrance is in Gétigné; a pedestrian entrance links to Clisson. Check the department's site for hours and prices.
new.q: Domaine de la Garenne Lemot, Avenue Xavier Rineau, Gétigné

new.title: Tour the medieval and Renaissance Château de Châteaubriant
new.desc: A medieval fortress is joined by a Renaissance residence begun from 1490 by Françoise de Dinan and Jean de Laval. The Loire-Atlantique department runs it as a Grand Patrimoine site.
new.tip: A one-hour guided tour runs year-round from February to December; hours vary by season. It is at Place Charles de Gaulle.
new.q: Château de Châteaubriant, Place Charles de Gaulle, Châteaubriant

new.title: Discover the Château d'Ancenis above the Loire
new.desc: The Château d'Ancenis has been classed a historic monument since 1977 and owned by the town since 1986. Its park is open daily and the Renaissance wing hosts temporary exhibitions.
new.tip: The park is free from 8:00 to 21:00. The exhibition in the Logis Renaissance runs Wednesday to Sunday with seasonal hours.
new.q: Château d'Ancenis, Ancenis

new.title: Spend a day at the Puy du Fou historical park
new.desc: Puy du Fou in Les Epesses stages large historical shows such as Les Vikings, Le Signe du Triomphe in a Gallo-Roman arena, Le Dernier Panache and L'Épée du Roi Arthur (new in 2025). Its walk-through shows and recreated villages make it one of France's top attractions.
new.tip: Buy tickets online and plan the show timetable on arrival. A full day is needed, and a two-day stay is worthwhile.
new.q: Puy du Fou, Les Epesses

new.title: Climb the keep of the Château de Noirmoutier
new.desc: The museum occupies the whitewashed donjon, once a landmark for sailors, and covers local history from prehistory to the Vendée War. It has more than 600 pieces of Jersey faience and the chair used for General d'Elbée's execution in 1794.
new.tip: The castle is in the town of Noirmoutier-en-l'Île near the port. Check opening hours, which vary by season.
new.q: Château de Noirmoutier, Place d'Armes, Noirmoutier-en-l'Île

new.title: Visit the Vieux Château on Île d'Yeu
new.desc: This medieval fortress stands on a rocky headland on the island's south-west coast. It is a listed monument and the island's top spot for nesting gulls; tradition says Hergé drew on it for the Black Island in Tintin.
new.tip: The 2026 programme lists 1.5-hour guided visits at 10:30 on some dates in May, June and September, booked via the tourist office (about 9 euros).
new.q: Vieux Château, L'Île-d'Yeu

new.title: Explore the ruins of Maillezais abbey
new.desc: The abbey was founded around 976 and moved to Maillezais in 1010, later becoming a cathedral. The Wars of Religion left impressive ruins, including the transept and nave walls and two towers flanking the portal.
new.tip: Allow 1.5 to 2 hours. Combine it with a boat trip from the embarcadère at the foot of the abbey.
new.q: Abbaye Saint-Pierre de Maillezais, Maillezais

new.title: Climb the Mélusine tower in Vouvant
new.desc: The 36 m Tour Mélusine is the only remaining part of the Lusignan castle at Vouvant, dating from the early 13th century. Legend credits the fairy Mélusine with building the castle in a night; the village is a Plus Beau Village de France.
new.tip: Buy tickets (about 3 euros) at the tourist office on place du Bail. The climb is 122 steps with views over the Mère valley.
new.q: Tour Mélusine, Vouvant

new.title: Tour the Renaissance Château de Terre-Neuve
new.desc: This Renaissance castle in Fontenay-le-Comte was built around 1580-1590 for Nicolas Rapin and has been a historic monument since 1978. The Vassé and Rochebrune family have owned it since 1805, and a museum of their collections opened in 2018.
new.tip: Check chateau-terreneuve.com for current visiting times and prices.
new.q: Château de Terre-Neuve, Fontenay-le-Comte

new.title: Walk the fortress of Tiffauges, Bluebeard's castle
new.desc: The Château de Tiffauges was a stronghold of Gilles de Rais in the mid-15th century and is often called the Bluebeard castle. Visitors can see the ruins and enjoy demonstrations such as trebuchet shows and medieval games.
new.tip: The keep itself cannot be visited. Some activities are by reservation only, so check the castle's website first.
new.q: Château de Tiffauges, Tiffauges

new.title: See the birthplaces of Clemenceau and de Lattre
new.desc: The national museum in Mouilleron-en-Pareds combines the birthplace of Georges Clemenceau and that of Marshal Jean de Lattre de Tassigny. Both houses carry the Maison des Illustres label and the museum replaced the old Musée des Deux Victoires.
new.tip: The museum is at 1 rue Plante Choux; check musee-clemenceau-delattre.fr for hours.
new.q: Musée national Clemenceau-de Lattre, Rue Plante Choux, Mouilleron-en-Pareds

new.title: Browse modern art at the Abbaye Sainte-Croix museum
new.desc: The museum of modern and contemporary art occupies a wing of a 17th-century Benedictine convent in Les Sables-d'Olonne. Its best-known holdings are works by Gaston Chaissac and Victor Brauner.
new.tip: Located on rue de Verdun; check lemasc.fr for opening times and exhibitions.
new.q: Musée de l'Abbaye Sainte-Croix, Rue de Verdun, Les Sables-d'Olonne

new.title: Cross Napoleon's pentagon at La Roche-sur-Yon
new.desc: Napoleon founded La Roche-sur-Yon on 25 May 1804 as the Vendée prefecture, with a pentagonal plan and a 2.8-hectare central square. An equestrian statue of Napoleon was inaugurated there on 20 August 1854.
new.tip: The square was redesigned and completed in 2013 with water features. It is free and best explored on foot.
new.q: Place Napoléon, La Roche-sur-Yon

new.title: Climb the Tour d'Arundel at La Chaume
new.desc: The tower is what remains of the 15th-century Château Saint-Clair, built by the princes of Talmont at the harbour entrance of Les Sables-d'Olonne. It carries a lighthouse light from 1855. After works, it reopened to visitors on 25 July 2026.
new.tip: Book the climb through the tourist offices or online. Check access before going as the reopening is recent.
new.q: Tour d'Arundel, La Chaume, Les Sables-d'Olonne

new.title: Discover the Carolingian abbey church of Déas
new.desc: The abbey church of Saint-Philbert-de-Grand-Lieu dates from around 815. It is noted for piers alternating white stone and brick and is one of the oldest churches in western France.
new.tip: The site is at 2 place de l'abbatiale. Check abbatialedeas.fr for hours and prices.
new.q: Abbatiale de Déas, Place de l'Abbatiale, Saint-Philbert-de-Grand-Lieu

new.title: Eat a buckwheat galette at Crêperie Les 2 Marais
new.desc: This crêperie sits on the Place du Vieux Marché behind the Collégiale Saint-Aubin, in the walled town of Guérande. Gault&Millau selected it in 2025 as a galette address in an austere stone building.
new.tip: Order a galette with local fleur de sel and a salted-butter caramel crêpe. The street number varies by source (2 or 4 place du Vieux Marché).
new.q: Crêperie Les 2 Marais, 2 Place du Vieux Marché, Guérande

new.title: Lunch at the Auberge de Kerhinet in a thatched cottage
new.desc: The inn is in the middle of the pedestrian hamlet of Kerhinet in the Brière park, run by chef Ludovic Favrel and his wife Isabelle. It serves traditional cuisine and also has five rooms.
new.tip: Payment was cash or cheque only in listings; confirm hours and booking on aubergedekerhinet.com.
new.q: Auberge de Kerhinet, Kerhinet, Saint-Lyphard

new.title: Try the catch of the day at L'Estacade, Le Croisic
new.desc: This hotel-restaurant at 4 quai du Lénigo on the port holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand (2024) and Plate (2025). Its menus follow the daily fish market, including a Terre et Océan menu.
new.tip: Book ahead for lunch in good weather. The port views are part of the appeal.
new.q: L'Estacade, 4 Quai du Lénigo, Le Croisic

new.title: Shop for seafood at the Halles de Saint-Nazaire
new.desc: The covered market on Place du Commerce was built between 1956 and 1958 and is one of the city's Reconstruction landmarks. It has about 35 stalls around 900 square metres, with fish on the north side and meat and charcuterie on the south.
new.tip: Go in the morning. Buy shellfish or smoked fish and picnic by the port.
new.q: Halles de Saint-Nazaire, Place du Commerce, Saint-Nazaire

new.title: Eat oysters and seafood at Cœur et Crème, Pornic
new.desc: This brasserie on quai Leray faces the old port and the château. It serves seafood platters and oysters opened by a professional shucker, with an all-you-can-eat seafood buffet on Fridays.
new.tip: Book for the Friday seafood buffet. Reviews rate the oysters and the port view.
new.q: Cœur et Crème, Quai Leray, Pornic

new.title: Taste local produce at Fleur de Sel, Noirmoutier
new.desc: This restaurant is rated 13/20 by Gault&Millau and run by chef Eric Pichou. It offers local, seasonal menus at 31 and 41 euros.
new.tip: Ask for island potatoes in season; the Bonnotte harvest lasts only about ten days in early May. Book ahead in summer.
new.q: Fleur de Sel, Noirmoutier-en-l'Île

new.title: Eat seafood at Viviers Rocheteau in La Chaume
new.desc: This seafood restaurant at 7 rue du Bargeouri in the La Chaume quarter has operated since 1900. A new team took over a few years ago while keeping the old character.
new.tip: Come for oysters and shellfish by the harbour. Reserve in summer.
new.q: Viviers Rocheteau, 7 Rue du Bargeouri, La Chaume, Les Sables-d'Olonne

new.title: Taste sardines at L'Atelier de la Sardine
new.desc: This shop-museum on the quay of Saint-Gilles-Croix-de-Vie, opposite the casino, tells the story of Conserverie Gendreau, the last Vendée cannery. The town is known for its sardine fishing and canning.
new.tip: Buy tinned local sardines. Spring 2024 hours were 10:00-18:00 daily; check before going.
new.q: L'Atelier de la Sardine, Saint-Gilles-Croix-de-Vie

new.title: Try goret mogettes at Les P'tits Ventres de Terre
new.desc: This restaurant opened in 1980 and is inspired by the Vendée hearths where mogette bean pots simmered for hours. Its signature dish is goret mogettes, a stew of pork and white beans.
new.tip: Address listed as 87 or 79 boulevard du Maréchal Leclerc, so check. Book for dinner.
new.q: Les P'tits Ventres de Terre, 87 Boulevard du Maréchal Leclerc, La Roche-sur-Yon

new.title: Visit Château du Coing, a Muscadet estate at Saint-Fiacre
new.desc: Château du Coing is an 18th-century château in Saint-Fiacre-sur-Maine, at the heart of Muscadet country. Its Italianate outbuildings, linked to the Clisson style of François-Frédéric Lemot, have been listed as historic monuments since 2018.
new.tip: Confirm tasting and visiting hours with the estate before you go, as they vary by season.
new.q: Château du Coing, Saint-Fiacre-sur-Maine

new.title: Sip gamay at Domaine Landron Chartier in Ancenis
new.desc: This family estate has made organic wines in the Coteaux d'Ancenis since 2002. It offers guided vineyard tastings and a shop in central Ancenis with free tastings.
new.tip: Try the fruity gamay red. Check opening hours for the shop.
new.q: La Boutique Landron Chartier, 51 Place Jeanne d'Arc, Ancenis

new.title: Eat galettes at Crêperie Le Chat Botté in Clisson
new.desc: Open since 1986 at 1 rue des Rémouleurs, this crêperie sits between the market hall and the castle. Reviewers praise its crispy galettes and friendly owner.
new.tip: Open Thursday to Saturday for lunch and dinner according to listings. Book ahead.
new.q: Crêperie Le Chat Botté, 1 Rue des Rémouleurs, Clisson

new.title: Order mussels at Le Bateau Ivre on Le Pouliguen port
new.desc: This crêperie-restaurant on the harbour is known for galettes, mussels and grilled sardines in season. Visitors describe it as simple, effective and friendly.
new.tip: Sit on the quay in summer and ask for the grilled sardines when in season.
new.q: Le Bateau Ivre, Port, Le Pouliguen

new.title: Eat galettes and seafood at Le Derwin, Batz-sur-Mer
new.desc: This crêperie is rated 11/20 by Gault&Millau for 2025, which recognises its galettes and the seafood it sources from a nearby fishmonger.
new.tip: Check hours and book for peak season.
new.q: Crêperie du Derwin, Allée du Dervin, Batz-sur-Mer

new.title: Dine at La Citadelle in Châteaubriant
new.desc: La Citadelle, on place de la Motte near the château, serves modern cuisine and appears in the Michelin Guide in the two-euro price band. A Michelin Plate has been reported for 2024-2025.
new.tip: Book ahead, especially at weekends.
new.q: La Citadelle, Place de la Motte, Châteaubriant

new.title: Book Les Bafouettes on Île d'Yeu
new.desc: This restaurant in Port-Joinville is the most cited table on the island. Reviewers mention tuna risotto and lobster on the menu.
new.tip: It sits a little back from the port; reserve in summer.
new.q: Les Bafouettes, Port-Joinville, L'Île-d'Yeu

new.title: Buy chocolates and shortbread at Le Chocolatier Sablais
new.desc: This artisan chocolatier at 14 rue Clément Ader in Les Sables-d'Olonne is run by Ségolène and Stéphane Arnauld. It sells chocolates, almond rochers and shortbread biscuits and offers guided visits.
new.tip: Ask about guided visits; hours vary by day.
new.q: Le Chocolatier Sablais, 14 Rue Clément Ader, Les Sables-d'Olonne

new.title: Dine at L'Ardoisine in Fontenay-le-Comte
new.desc: This restaurant on rue des Halles serves traditional French cuisine revisited by chef Denis Marxer in the historic centre.
new.tip: Reserve ahead for dinner.
new.q: L'Ardoisine, Rue des Halles, Fontenay-le-Comte

new.title: Walk the Guérande salt pans with a paludier
new.desc: Terre de Sel at Pradel, part of the Salines de Guérande cooperative, offers about fifteen guided walks of 45 minutes to 2 hours around the salt pans. Guides are paludiers or naturalists, and there is a panoramic terrace over the Guérande basin.
new.tip: A working-saline visit with fleur de sel tasting runs from April to September. Check terredesel.fr or call 02 40 62 08 80.
new.q: Terre de Sel, Pradel, Guérande

new.title: Meet marine life at the Océarium du Croisic
new.desc: The aquarium on avenue de Saint-Goustan opened in 1992 and has 56 tanks. About 2,500 cubic metres of seawater house several oceans, including a coral lagoon.
new.tip: Open most days with some closures in January. Check prices on the official site.
new.q: Océarium du Croisic, Avenue de Saint-Goustan, Le Croisic

new.title: Glide through the Brière marsh in a chaland
new.desc: Local boatmen run commented chaland (flat-bottomed boat) trips from Fédrun island and Bréca port in Saint-Joachim, about 45 minutes to an hour, on the fauna, flora and traditions of the marsh.
new.tip: Book with a provider such as Valérie Aoustin-Huard, who departs from Fédrun. Combine with a calèche ride from Bréca.
new.q: Île de Fédrun, Saint-Joachim

new.title: Watch the Cinéscénie night show at Puy du Fou
new.desc: La Cinéscénie is a vast night spectacle at Puy du Fou, billed as the largest night show in the world. The 2026 season ran on Friday and Saturday evenings from 6 June to 12 September.
new.tip: Book tickets in advance and wear warm clothing for the late show.
new.q: Cinéscénie du Puy du Fou, Les Epesses

new.title: Hike the Côte Sauvage on the GR34
new.desc: The Côte Sauvage runs about 14 km along the GR34 customs path from the Tréhic jetty at Le Croisic past Batz-sur-Mer to Penchâteau point at Le Pouliguen. An 8 km circuit starts from Place du Général de Gaulle in Le Croisic.
new.tip: The path is pedestrian only. Allow time for a stop at a rocky cove.
new.q: Croix des Douaniers, Côte Sauvage, Le Croisic

new.title: Walk the Pornic customs path to Gourmalon
new.desc: The coast path links the Pointe de Gourmalon, the Noëveillard cornice and the Anse aux Lapins. Views reach the Bay of Bourgneuf and Noirmoutier, and fishing huts on stilts line the shore.
new.tip: Go late in the afternoon for sunset. A loop of about 8.4 km starts from Pornic.
new.q: Pointe de Gourmalon, Pornic

new.title: Stroll the Remblai and Vendée Globe Walk of Fame
new.desc: Les Sables-d'Olonne has hosted the start and finish of the Vendée Globe since 1989. On the Remblai, nine plaques honour the race winners between the Atlantes and rue de la Plage.
new.tip: The channel jetties are the best viewpoint on race days. Free to walk.
new.q: Remblai, Les Sables-d'Olonne

new.title: Walk to the Pointe des Dames lighthouse on Noirmoutier
new.desc: The Phare de la pointe des Dames stands at the northern tip of the island of Noirmoutier, close to Noirmoutier-en-l'Île. A menhir marks the same headland, making it an easy coastal stop on foot or by bike.
new.tip: Go at low tide or sunset for the best light over the water, and bring a windproof layer as the point is exposed.
new.q: Phare de la pointe des Dames, Noirmoutier-en-l'Île

new.title: Cycle the Côte Sauvage to Port de la Meule on Yeu
new.desc: A ride of about 20 to 35 km follows Île d'Yeu's granite wild coast to Port de la Meule, the only real refuge on that coast, with a chapel above it.
new.tip: Rent bikes at the ferry exits in Port-Joinville. Go early in summer.
new.q: Port de la Meule, L'Île-d'Yeu

new.title: Row through the Venise Verte from Maillezais
new.desc: The Embarcadère de l'Abbaye at the foot of the abbey has run since 1963 as the Marais poitevin's only association-run landing stage. It offers guided and row-yourself trips, including a three-hour trip.
new.tip: The landing stage is at rue du Grand Port; call 02 51 87 21 87. Prices vary by boat and guide.
new.q: Embarcadère de l'Abbaye, Rue du Grand Port, Maillezais

new.title: Headbang at Hellfest in Clisson
new.desc: Hellfest runs each June in Clisson. The 2026 edition ran from 18 to 21 June with 183 acts on six stages.
new.tip: Buy tickets far in advance as the festival sells out fast. Stay in Clisson or nearby.
new.q: Hellfest, Clisson

new.title: Browse the Guérande market on Wednesday or Saturday
new.desc: The main food market runs on Wednesday and Saturday mornings inside the walls, from 8:00 to 13:00, under the covered halls and on Place Saint-Aubin and rue Vannetaise.
new.tip: Buy fleur de sel and local produce. Come on Saturday for the biggest market.
new.q: Marché de Guérande, Place Saint-Aubin, Guérande

new.title: Swim at Saint-Brevin's Plage de l'Océan
new.desc: The Océan beach runs along the seafront promenade of Saint-Brevin-les-Pins. A shore path leads to Mindin and the Serpent d'océan, and four beaches are supervised in summer.
new.tip: Combine a swim with the 11.7 km Mindin loop.
new.q: Plage de l'Océan, Saint-Brevin-les-Pins

new.title: Cycle La Vélodyssée from Jard to La Tranche
new.desc: The Jard-sur-Mer to La Tranche-sur-Mer stage of La Vélodyssée (EuroVelo 1) is about 18.6 km. It alternates paved paths and forest tracks, with detours to the Conches and Rocher beaches.
new.tip: The route is easy; stop at Plage des Conches.
new.q: Jard-sur-Mer

new.title: Swim along the 9 km bay of La Baule
new.desc: La Baule's great beach unrolls fine sand in an arc for 9 km between Pornichet and Le Pouliguen. The bay has been ranked among the world's most beautiful bays since 2011 and the sand is cleaned daily in season.
new.tip: It gets crowded in July and August. Come in June or September.
new.q: Plage de La Baule, La Baule-Escoublac

new.title: Step aboard a liner at Escal'Atlantic in Saint-Nazaire
new.desc: Escal'Atlantic is an immersive museum inside the former German submarine base on the Saint-Nazaire waterfront. It recreates the decks and cabins of the great ocean liners.
new.tip: Combine it with a walk on the roof of the Base sous-marine for views over the port.
new.q: Escal'Atlantic, Boulevard de la Légion d'Honneur, Saint-Nazaire

new.title: Join the Fête de la Sardine at Saint-Gilles-Croix-de-Vie
new.desc: The summer festival on the port celebrates the town's sardine fishing and includes a guided tour of the Gendreau cannery. The 2026 listing gave 26 July with free entry.
new.tip: Check the date each year with the tourist office.
new.q: Port de Saint-Gilles-Croix-de-Vie

new.title: Browse the Marché des Pins in Saint-Brevin
new.desc: This traditional market runs on Thursday and Sunday mornings in the centre of Les Pins at Place Henri Baslé. The seaside town also has a Saturday market in the Océan quarter.
new.tip: Go on Sunday morning. Check the town hall for current days.
new.q: Marché des Pins, Place Henri Baslé, Saint-Brevin-les-Pins

new.title: Walk the Ker circuit from Kerhinet to Bréca
new.desc: This marked walk links the thatched village of Kerhinet to the boat landing of Bréca across the Brière marshes. The route passes traditional villages of the park.
new.tip: Wear waterproof shoes after rain. The walk is outdoors and free.
new.q: Kerhinet, Saint-Lyphard

new.title: Tour the Chantiers de l'Atlantique shipyard
new.desc: Guided tours visit the Saint-Nazaire yard where cruise liners are built. Tours are offered in French and English and listed by the tourist office.
new.tip: Booking is required and tours can be combined with Escal'Atlantic.
new.q: Chantiers de l'Atlantique, Saint-Nazaire

new.title: Shop the Halles Centrales market in Les Sables-d'Olonne
new.desc: The market in Baltard-style halls shows Vendée produce from Tuesday to Sunday morning. The halls were under works from February 2025 to summer 2026, with traders at temporary halls on Place Louis Guédon.
new.tip: Check the market's current location with the town hall.
new.q: Halles Centrales, Les Sables-d'Olonne

new.title: Cross the Passage du Gois at low tide
new.desc: The Passage du Gois is a tidal causeway to Noirmoutier. It is passable roughly 1.5 hours either side of low tide, and the window widens when the coefficient exceeds 70.
new.tip: Check the tide table before crossing; GPS ignores the tides. On foot or by bike, only at low tide.
new.q: Passage du Gois, Beauvoir-sur-Mer
